conditions.exact_rule_quote: sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises
conditions.description: The tenant engaged in at least one covered transfer-of-possession act as to the whole or any part of the premises.
conditions.scope: Section 14(1)(b) covered conduct only: sub-letting, assignment, or otherwise parting with possession of all or part of the premises.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: on or after the 9th day of June, 1952
conditions.description: The covered conduct occurred on or after 9 June 1952.
conditions.scope: Post-9-June-1952 conduct; section 16(1) supplies the contrasting pre-9-June-1952 deeming rule.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord
conditions.description: The covered post-1952 conduct occurred without legally sufficient landlord consent in writing.
conditions.scope: Written landlord consent for the relevant post-1952 sub-letting; section 16(2)-(3) supplies the related written-consent constraint.

bindings.reason: The tenant's written statement admitted Hans Raj and Ram Bakhsh were sub-tenants in different portions, supporting the covered-conduct proposition while leaving legal effect unresolved.

bindings.stage: second appeal record recounting affidavit admission
bindings.reason: The tenant's affidavit admission specifically states that he sublet identified rooms to Hans Raj and Ram Bakhsh, directly supporting the covered-conduct proposition.

bindings.stage: second appeal record recounting affidavit admission
bindings.reason: The admission dates the two sub-lettings to 1963 and 1964, supporting the post-9-June-1952 temporal condition.
The landlords alleged that the 1963-64 inductions occurred without written landlord consent; this is a supporting allegation, not an established target fact.

The landlords asserted that Ex. A-7 did not amount to written consent and alternatively that any authority lasted only 11 months; both propositions support the absence-of-effective-written-consent condition if accepted.
The tenant pleaded that Ex. A-7 gave him the right to sub-let; if legally effective as written landlord consent, that proposition would defeat c3.

The appellant argued that the tenancy and the asserted written sub-letting consent continued until May 31, 1970; if accepted, that would defeat the absence-of-effective-written-consent condition for the 1963-64 sub-lettings.
The appellant alternatively argued that the asserted written consent in Ex. A-7 carried into statutory tenancy and covered the 1963-64 sub-tenancies; if accepted, that would defeat c3.
